title: Vindaloo
subtitle: Goan hot and sour pork curry
excerpt: The fiery Goan curry derived from the Portuguese dish carne de vinha d'alhos: pork marinated in chilli, vinegar, and garlic, then slow-cooked until the sauce is thick, red, and intensely sour-hot. Not simply a test of heat tolerance but a complex, well-balanced dish.

recipe.sourceNotes: Vindaloo derives from the Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos (meat in wine and garlic), brought to Goa when it was a Portuguese colony from 1510 to 1961. The original Portuguese dish used wine vinegar; Goan cooks substituted palm or cider vinegar, added the chillies and spices of Indian cooking, and created something new. The name evolved from vinha d'alhos to vindaloo. The defining character is the vinegar: it provides the sourness that balances the heat from the chillies and the fat of the pork. British curry house vindaloo, served primarily as a heat challenge, is a simplified version; the authentic Goan dish is sour, aromatic, and complex. The overnight marinade is traditional and produces a more integrated flavour.

content.text: The vinegar marinade tenderises the pork as well as flavouring it; overnight is traditional. The finished sauce should be thick enough to coat the back of a spoon, with the oil beginning to separate at the edges. That separation is the sign the curry is ready.

items.preparation: boneless shoulder preferred; cut into 4 cm chunks
dried Kashmiri chillies or similar medium-heat dried chillies; soaked in warm water for 20 minutes, then blended with the vinegar

content.text: Blend the soaked chillies with the vinegar, garlic, and ginger to a smooth paste. Mix with the ground spices. Toss the pork in this marinade, cover, and refrigerate overnight or for at least 4 hours.

Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Cook the onions for 15 minutes until deep golden. Add the marinated pork with all the marinade. Cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the marinade has dried out and the pork is beginning to fry in the oil.

Add the tinned tomatoes and 200 ml of water. Season with salt and sugar. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook for 60 to 75 minutes until the pork is completely tender and the sauce is thick. Remove the lid for the last 15 minutes. Serve with basmati rice.
